conflicts: Curry 2009 (arc-intensity scaling) vs NIST ASD (reference code T8748, accuracy B+) for the 29 drawn lines that both give: A(Curry)/A(NIST) ranges 0.36-2.47, median 0.72. i.e. the two sets agree only within a factor of about 2.5 either way, so the entered Curry values (given only for lines without a NIST A) are rough; largest ratio 465.0509 nm: 4.00e+07 vs 1.62e+07 s-1
isotopic abundances: NIST gives 136Ce 0.185(2) %, 140Ce 88.450(51) %; the IAEA LiveChart record gives 0.186(2) % and 88.449(51) % (rounding of the same evaluation); NIST values entered
not_found: level lifetimes: Den Hartog, Buettner, Lawler, J. Phys. B 42, 085006 (2009) measured 153 Ce I levels (150 even, 3 odd) to +-5 % - only the abstract (osti.gov) could be opened; the publisher page was blocked by a bot check on four attempts and no open copy was found. Xu et al., "Radiative lifetimes in Ce I and Ce II", Eur. Phys. J. D (2003), doi:10.1140/epjd/e2003-00054-4, measured 18 even levels between 26545 and 29102 cm-1 (abstract only; above the drawn levels). Li et al., Phys. Rev. A 62, 032505 (2000): two Ce I levels, abstract only

isotope shifts: measured by Champeau & Verges, Physica B+C 83, 373 (1976) (140-142 and 136-140, eight infrared lines), Thayer et al. (2003, crossed-beam, natural Ce) and Ankush, Ahmad, Deo, JQSRT (2021, 555-833 nm Fourier-transform); only abstracts without numbers could be opened
hyperfine structure: none for the stable isotopes (all four have I = 0)
precise (laser/comb) transition frequencies, branching ratios, reduced matrix elements: none located beyond what NIST carries
laser cooling or precision-spectroscopy use of neutral Ce: none located
the 5029-line table of Nitz et al., J. Phys. B 51, 045007 (2018) is an online supplement that could not be downloaded; only the paper text was read
notes: No level entry carries new data: the stable Ce isotopes have nuclear spin 0 (no hyperfine structure) and the lifetime papers could not be opened. The 32 transitions listed are lines between drawn levels for which NIST gives no A; the A values come from Curry 2009 (PDF from the NIST publication server, parsed as text) and are semi-empirical arc-intensity values with +-35 % stated uncertainty, likely biased high (see conflicts). Wavelengths in the labels are the air wavelengths printed in that table (from the unpublished Martin line list).
